args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. The release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been marked unhealthy in staging. Mitigation: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and check why it was promoted even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** Every region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) was running v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Because it has been healthy in production before, rolling back to it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Result:** All three regions now run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also lists follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already been marked unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
